# GitHub Actions — Android APK builds

`build-apk.yml` is the only **Android build** workflow in this repository. It produces installable debug and release APKs for both native clients without requiring a local Android SDK. The earlier `main` workflow `android.yml` and its `mobile/` app were removed during consolidation; there is no longer a second, conflicting "Build Android APK" job.

`publish-release.yml` is a small release helper, not another build: it can attach already-uploaded phone/TV APK artifacts from a specified Actions run to an existing tag via `repository_dispatch` or `workflow_dispatch`.

## Triggers

- `push` to `main`
- `push` to `arena/69ba68a7-hallyu-stream`
- `push` of a `v*` tag
- `pull_request` targeting `main`
- manual `workflow_dispatch`

Tag pushes matching `v*` additionally attach the built APKs to a GitHub Release as direct `.apk` assets. Prefer those Release assets over the zipped Actions artifacts: artifact blob downloads can be blocked by network egress rules even when the run is green.

The two build jobs deliberately rename their outputs before upload:

```text
hallyu-stream-phone-debug.apk    hallyu-stream-phone-release.apk
hallyu-stream-tv-debug.apk       hallyu-stream-tv-release.apk
```

Both Gradle projects otherwise produce `app-debug.apk` / `app-release.apk`; with `merge-multiple: true` in the release job those identical names would overwrite each other and only one client's APKs would reach the Release. The first `v0.1.0` tag demonstrated exactly that, so its release and tag were deleted; `v0.1.1` carries all four correctly named assets.

## Publishing from an existing run

If a tag build completes its APK jobs but its `release` step is interrupted, `publish-release.yml` can publish those already-uploaded artifacts without another 18-minute Gradle build:

```bash
gh api -X POST repos/halluyapp/hallyu-stream/dispatches \
  -f event_type=publish-apks \
  -F client_payload[run_id]=41519431805 \
  -F client_payload[tag]=v0.1.1
```

It downloads `hallyu-stream-*-apk-*` from that run, verifies `.apk` files exist, then calls `softprops/action-gh-release@v2` with `contents: write`. This is how the [v0.1.1 Release](https://github.com/halluyapp/hallyu-stream/releases/tag/v0.1.1) was published after the `v0.1.1` tag run was cancelled.

## What each job does

| Job | Command highlights | Output artifact |
|---|---|---|
| `verify` | `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run smoke`, `npm run build:preview` | `hallyu-stream-preview-dist-<sha>` |
| `build-mobile-apk` | `npm ci --prefix apps/mobile`, `npx expo prebuild --platform android --clean`, `./gradlew assembleDebug`, then signed `./gradlew assembleRelease` | `hallyu-stream-mobile-apk-<sha>` |
| `build-tv-apk` | `npm ci --prefix apps/tv`, write `apps/tv/.env`, `gradle --project-dir apps/tv/android assembleDebug assembleRelease` | `hallyu-stream-tv-apk-<sha>` |
| `release` | download both APK artifacts, `softprops/action-gh-release@v2` | GitHub Release assets |

## Toolchain installed on the runner

- Node 20 with npm cache from `package-lock.json`
- Temurin JDK 17
- Android SDK: `platform-tools`, `platforms;android-34`, `platforms;android-35`, `build-tools;34.0.0`, `build-tools;35.0.0`, `ndk;26.1.10909125`
- Gradle 8.10.2 via `gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v3` (matches the Expo-generated phone wrapper)

The phone build uses the wrapper generated by `expo prebuild` (Gradle 8.10.2); the TV build uses the setup Gradle directly because `apps/tv/android` has no committed wrapper jar. Both native apps have committed `package-lock.json` files, so CI uses `npm ci` for deterministic installs. The TV app pins `react-native-config@1.5.3` because newer releases do not autolink against the React Native 0.76 community CLI used here.

CI also patches the generated phone project after prebuild: the Kotlin Gradle plugin is pinned to `1.9.25` (Expo SDK 52's Compose compiler requires it, while the RN version catalog defaults to `1.9.24`) and Gradle heap is raised to 4 GB. The TV project disables Jetifier and uses the same 4 GB heap; Jetifier runs out of memory transforming the large `react-native-tvos` AAR.

Native modules are pinned to the Expo SDK 52 / React Native 0.76 compatible set (`react-native-svg@15.8.0`, `react-native-video@6.9.0`, `react-native-qrcode-svg@6.3.0`, `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage@2.1.0`). Floating `^` ranges resolved to newer releases whose generated Paper interfaces require `ViewManagerWithGeneratedInterface`, which RN 0.76.5 does not provide. The phone app also declares `expo-asset@11.0.5` explicitly: `@expo/metro-config` resolves `expo-asset/tools/hashAssetFiles` from the project root during release JS bundling, and Expo's own nested copy is not enough.

## Signing

Both jobs generate a throwaway keystore in `$RUNNER_TEMP` with `keytool`. The phone release build receives AGP injected signing properties:

```text
-Pandroid.injected.signing.store.file
-Pandroid.injected.signing.store.password
-Pandroid.injected.signing.key.alias
-Pandroid.injected.signing.key.password
```

The TV release build reads the equivalent `HALLYU_SIGNING_STORE_FILE`, `HALLYU_SIGNING_STORE_PASSWORD`, `HALLYU_SIGNING_KEY_ALIAS`, `HALLYU_SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD` environment variables in `apps/tv/android/app/build.gradle`.

**This ephemeral key is for CI artifacts only.** Before Play Store / sideload distribution, supply a persistent production keystore through protected secrets and update the signing configuration. Never commit a keystore, password, or service-role key.

## Configuration variables

All are optional GitHub Actions repository variables, not secrets. Absent values degrade gracefully to empty config, so pairing screens show honest errors instead of fake approval.

Phone reads `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` at Expo prebuild/bundle time. TV reads `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `PAIRING_CLIENT_KEY`, `ZAR_BASE_URL`, `MOVIE_SEASON`, `MOVIE_EPISODE` from `apps/tv/.env`; each falls back to the matching `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` variable.

- Workflow YAML parsed with PyYAML.
- Workflow validated with `@action-validator/cli`.
- Root strict typecheck, smoke test, and preview production build pass locally.
- GitHub Actions [run 41509904497](https://github.com/halluyapp/hallyu-stream/actions/runs/41509904497) completed successfully on `68f2f75`, uploading debug + release APK artifacts for both phone and TV clients.
- GitHub Actions [run 41514853664](https://github.com/halluyapp/hallyu-stream/actions/runs/41514853664) completed successfully on `ca03757` after a clean push-triggered re-run: `verify`, `build-mobile-apk` and `build-tv-apk` all passed.
- GitHub Actions [run 41521621257](https://github.com/halluyapp/hallyu-stream/actions/runs/41521621257) successfully published the four corrected `.apk` assets to the `v0.1.1` Release.

No Android build has run in this sandbox (no Java / Android SDK); APKs are produced exclusively by the GitHub Actions runner. The artifacts are CI builds, not store-ready signed releases.
